setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, where the technology policy sets rules for records, recordings and tools.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you use workplace technology under a policy that sets rules for how it is used.
detail: Your station is near the front.
pressure: {coworker3} says the policy is just a formality.
You are in a hurry to finish before break.

tiers.1: Looking at records you have no work reason to see harms the people in them.
tiers.2: Recording people needs their agreement before it starts.
tiers.3: Internal conversations stay inside the workplace unless the policy says otherwise.
tiers.4: Use only materials the workplace has permission to use.
tiers.5: Check anything a tool writes before it goes out under your name.

fact: You can open records of people you do not work with, and the policy says records are opened only for assigned tasks.
issues.short: the record you have no task for
issues.action: Close the record and keep to your assigned tasks.
issues.brief: close the record and stick to your tasks
issues.reason: Access is recorded, and people trust the workplace to protect their records from curiosity.
issues.lesson: Open records only for your assigned tasks, even when nothing stops you.

shortcut.text: Look just once out of curiosity, since nobody checks who opens records.
shortcut.brief: look at the record once out of curiosity
shortcut.why: The policy limits access to assigned tasks, and the system keeps a log of who looked.
shortcut.mis: Access that goes unnoticed is allowed.

clear: You already closed a record you had no task for without reading it.

fact: {coworker} suggests secretly recording a meeting on a phone, and the policy says recordings need everyone's agreement.
issues.action: Decline, and suggest asking everyone for agreement or taking written notes.
issues.reason: Recording without agreement breaks the policy and the trust of the people in the meeting.
issues.lesson: Record people only with their agreement, or take written notes instead.

shortcut.text: Record it quietly, since it is only for your own notes.
shortcut.why: The policy needs everyone's agreement, and a private recording can still be shared by mistake.
shortcut.mis: A recording for personal use needs no one's agreement.

clear: Everyone in a meeting already agreed to have it recorded.
issues.done: everyone already agreed to the recording

fact: You want to post a screenshot of an internal chat on social media, and the policy says internal chats stay inside the workplace.
issues.short: the screenshot of the internal chat
issues.action: Skip the post, or describe your point without sharing the chat.
issues.brief: skip the post or describe it without the chat
issues.reason: An internal chat can hold details that were meant for coworkers only, even when it seems harmless.
issues.lesson: Keep internal conversations inside the workplace, even when you only want to share a funny moment.

shortcut.text: Post it with the names blurred, since nobody will be identified.
shortcut.brief: post the screenshot with names blurred
shortcut.why: A blurred screenshot still shares internal information that the policy keeps inside.

clear: You already deleted your draft post of an internal chat screenshot.
issues.done: the screenshot post is already dropped

fact: You want to put a website photo on a flyer, and the guide allows only images the workplace has permission to use.
issues.short: the website photo for the flyer
issues.action: Use an image the workplace has permission for, or ask {lead|the} to confirm.
issues.brief: use a cleared image or ask {lead|the}
issues.reason: Having permission is what the guide requires, and a quick question settles whether the photo qualifies.
issues.lesson: Use only images and materials the workplace has permission to use.

shortcut.text: Use the photo and credit the website underneath it.
shortcut.brief: use the photo and credit the website
shortcut.why: Credit does not replace permission, which is what the guide asks for.
shortcut.mis: Naming the source makes any image fair to use.

clear: {Lead|the} already confirmed the workplace has permission to use a website photo.

fact: You used a writing tool to draft a customer message, and the policy says staff are responsible for anything they send.
issues.short: the draft written by a tool
issues.action: Read and correct the draft before sending it, since you are responsible for it.
issues.reason: A tool can get details wrong or sound sure when it is not, and you answer for what goes out.
issues.lesson: Check anything a tool writes before it goes out under your name.

shortcut.text: Send it as written, since the tool is built to write well.
shortcut.why: Tools can make errors, and the policy makes you responsible for what you send.
shortcut.mis: A tool's draft needs no review.

clear: You already checked and corrected a customer message drafted by a tool.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves a technology rule that applies to you.
proceed.lesson: The technology policy applies to what you open, record, share, copy and send.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and do the same.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the policy, and it may break the rule.

generic.text: Do it now and mention it to {lead|the} afterward.
generic.why: The policy sets the rule beforehand, and telling someone later does not undo a breach.
generic.mis: It is easier to ask forgiveness than permission.

overcaution.text: Stop using all workplace technology until {lead|the} reviews the whole policy with you.
overcaution.why: The concern is specific. Stopping everything delays work the policy allows.
overcaution.mis: Any rule question means stopping all technology use.

setup: You want to add an outside photo to a flyer your team is preparing.

steps.text: Find a photo that fits the flyer
Add the photo to the flyer

rel: You need a specific photo before you can check it.
Permission comes before the photo goes on the flyer.
The finished flyer includes the photo.
process.lesson: Choose the image, confirm permission, place it, then share the result.

title: Technology reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it is posted near the computers.
prompt: Which line gives advice that breaks the policy?
doc.lesson: Technology reminders must match the workplace policy on records, recordings, chats, images and drafts.

lines.text: Open records only when your assigned task needs them.
lines.fine: Limits access to a work reason.

bad.text: Open any record you can reach if you are curious.
bad.why: Access is limited to assigned tasks, however easy it is to reach other records.

lines.text: Record a meeting only when everyone has agreed.

bad.text: Record a meeting quietly if the recording is only for you.
bad.why: Everyone's agreement is needed, even when the recording is private.

lines.text: Keep internal chats inside the workplace.

bad.text: Share an internal chat online if you hide the names.
bad.why: The details still leave the workplace, so hiding names does not make it allowed.

lines.text: Check anything a tool writes before you send it.
lines.fine: Makes you responsible for what goes out.

review.notes: All rules are stated as this workplace's policy; no recording or image-use law is cited. Tiers: records, recordings, internal chats, cleared materials, tool drafts.
